title: Redwood Security & Data Handling Review - Acme Health
summary: Review of Redwood's security posture and data handling controls for healthcare workloads. Focus on SOC 2/ISO artifacts, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, data residency, encryption/KMS and explicit confirmation about prompt retention, PII/PHI handling, and whether customer data is used for training. Redwood confirmed SOC2 Type II, offered private VPC / on-prem options, customer-managed KMS, and a data retention opt-out. Action items include sharing SOC2 report, encryption architecture diagram, and scheduling pilot discussion for private deployment.
topics: SOC 2 Type II and ISO certs
Encryption at rest and in transit; KMS/HSM
next_steps: Jordan to send SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 artifacts (link + redactions) by 2025-09-15
Priya to share KMS/encryption architecture diagram and data flow doc by 2025-09-17
Schedule follow-up deep dive on private/VPC deployment options w/ infra team week of 2025-09-22
Provide retention configuration options and sample audit logs export (anonymized)
Set up technical pilot: private deployment trial + KMS integration (target start 2025-10-01)
action_items: Owner: Jordan Lee; Item: Attach SOC 2 Type II report and short control mapping to Acme's checklist; Due: 2025-09-15
Owner: Priya Nair; Item: Provide KMS/HSM integration diagram and sample key rotation policy; Due: 2025-09-17
Owner: Marcus Chen; Item: Prepare checklist for PII/PHI handling and BAA guidance; Due: 2025-09-18
Owner: Ethan White (customer); Item: Share Acme's required retention windows and compliance questions matrix; Due: 2025-09-16
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-10 14:00 UTC | Duration: 47m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood Security SE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Sofia (CISO, Acme), Ethan (Cloud Security), Dr. Rina (Compliance)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time — we'll run through our security posture and specifically the data handling questions you sent over. Priya and Marcus are here for deep dives on encryption and private deploy.
[00:18] Sofia: Thanks. Short context: Acme Health handles PHI; main asks are around prompt retention, PII/PHI safeguards, and explicit confirmation that data won't be used to train models. Also we need SOC 2 artifacts and details on KMS.
[00:35] Priya: Totally, I'll start with SOC 2/ISO. Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II for the inference platform and ISO27001 certificate; we can send redacted reports. Controls cover change mgmt, incident response, encryption, and access control.
[00:52] Dr. Rina: When you say "cover encryption" can you be specific on key ownership and HSM support?
[00:59] Marcus: Sure. We support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Google KMS) and can integrate with on-prem HSMs for Private deployments. For hosted customers we offer envelope encryption: data encrypted at rest with service keys, and an option to bring-your-own-key (BYOK) so the customer controls the master key.
[01:20] Ethan: And rotation? Is that automatic or do we trigger it?
[01:24] Marcus: Key rotation is supported both ways. For BYOK, rotation policies can be enforced from your KMS. We provide guidance and sample policies; we'll share the architecture diagram after the call.
[01:36] Sofia: About data residency — Acme needs EU-only storage for certain workloads and effec- excuse me — for European patients. Can Redwood ensure region locking?
[01:49] Priya: Yes, region pinning is supported in Dedicated and Hosted with data region controls; for higher assurance we recommend Private VPC deployments which keep control plane and data plane inside your VPC/region.
[02:05] Jordan: One common question is audit logs — we produce request-level audit logs with token, route, model, and a hashed request id. Retention defaults to 90 days but can be extended; we can also export logs to your SIEM.
[02:23] Ethan: Are the logs PII-free by default or do they include prompt content? That's critical.
[02:29] Priya: Default logs include metadata and hashed identifiers, not full prompt text unless you enable full-text logging. For healthcare workloads we recommend disabling full-text retention on hosted. For Private you control the logging.
[02:45] Dr. Rina: And is there an explicit "no training" guarantee? Some vendors say they don't use customer data unless opted-in. We need an affirmative contractual statement.
[02:55] Jordan: Yes — Redwood does not use customer prompts or content to train underlying models. We have a policy and contract language that states we do not incorporate customer data into model training. We'll provide the exact clause for your legal.
[03:09] Sofia: Is that true for all tiers — hosted, dedicated, and private?
[03:13] Priya: For Hosted and Dedicated we provide the same no-training guarantee; for Private/on-prem the customer has full control and data never leaves the environment unless configured. Note: some open-source model variants can be run with telemetry disabled.
[03:29] Ethan: If we run a pilot on hosted initially, what are the switches to opt out of retention? Can we ensure prompts are deleted immediately?
[03:36] Marcus: There's a retention config. You can set prompt retention = 0 for no retention for logs/requests, and we also support an API flag to mark requests as non-retainable. For compliance, we can add a contract addendum to enforce retention policies.
[03:52] Dr. Rina: For PHI, we also need to know about BAAs. Does Redwood sign BAAs?
[03:58] Jordan: We do sign BAAs for customers with regulated healthcare workloads. We have a standard BAA and can include Private deployment controls as needed. We'll loop legal to send a draft.
[04:10] Sofia: About RBAC and SSO — we need SCIM provisioning, SAML SSO, and fine-grained RBAC to limit who can view logs and keys.
[04:20] Priya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is role-based with predefined roles (admin, dev, ops, auditor) and custom role support for dedicated/private customers. Audit logs track console and API actions; we also offer session recording hooks for dedicated setups.
[04:40] Ethan: Can audit logs be forwarded to our Splunk/CloudWatch? We want SIEM integration with preserved timestamps and integrity checks.
[04:47] Marcus: Yes — we provide streaming export to your SIEM, and logs include integrity checks (signed entries) for tamper-evidence. We'll share sample export schema.
[04:58] Sofia: Encryption in transit — TLS mutual auth?
[05:01] Priya: Standard TLS 1.2/1.3 for hosted; for Private we can enable mTLS between services and your gateways.
[05:10] Jordan: I want to circle back to "no training on customer data" wording — Priya has the legal text?
[05:16] Priya: I do. The clause: "Redwood will not use Customer Data to train or improve Models, without Customer's explicit written consent." We'll include the clause in the packet.
[05:28] Dr. Rina: Great. One more: PII/PHI detection — do you offer auto redaction or PII classifiers?
[05:34] Marcus: We have optional pre-processing modules: PII/PHI detection and redaction patterns (regex + ML detectors). For PHI we recommend pre-send redaction or routing to a Private deployment where redaction is applied in your VPC. We'll share the plugin docs.
[05:50] Ethan: If we need to keep prompt examples for evaluation, can we store them in a separate encrypted bucket with restricted access?
[05:57] Marcus: Yes — you can configure logs and artifacts to be exported to your own encrypted buckets and control IAM. That is the recommended pattern for eval datasets.
[06:06] Sofia: Are there known gaps or controls you don't provide out of the box? We want to map to our checklist.
[06:12] Priya: We try to be comprehensive, but things like SOC 2 mapping to specific HITRUST controls may need additional documentation. Also some advanced HSM integrations might need engineering scoping for on-prem HSM vendors. We'll do a controls mapping as an artifact.
[06:29] Jordan: Ok next steps — we'll send the SOC 2 and ISO artifacts, encryption diagrams, sample audit logs, and a BAA draft. Marcus will prep the PII/PHI redaction docs. Then schedule the pilot planning call.
[06:42] Sofia: Sounds good. Any open questions from Redwood?
[06:45] Jordan: No, just to confirm timeline — sending docs by mid next week.
[06:49] Ethan: We'll review and come back with retention windows and any additional legal asks.
[06:53] Dr. Rina: Thanks all.

[End of transcript]
questions: Do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 artifacts?
Can Redwood guarantee no training on customer data across tiers?
What are the retention configuration options and how to disable prompt retention?
Do you support BYOK and on-prem HSMs?
Can audit logs be exported to our SIEM with tamper-evidence?
Does Redwood sign BAAs for PHI workloads?
